payload.rationale: As of the September 19, 2026 cutoff, the official film site advertises a firm December 18, 2026 North American/IMAX release, December 16 international start, and specific early-access screenings on December 14–15. Scheduling fan-event screenings and IMAX dates roughly three months out signals that marketing, exhibitor bookings, and post-production are locked. Historically, major studio tentpoles very rarely move once inside the final ~90 days absent extraordinary shocks (pandemic-scale closures, industry strikes, catastrophic VFX shortfalls); the base rate for such late slips is on the order of a few percent. Principal photography for this film reportedly wrapped in 2025, leaving ample post-production time, and the December holiday corridor is a deliberate, strategically chosen slot that Warner Bros./Legendary would be reluctant to vacate. Only a delay beyond December 18 counts; earlier moves or the early-access screenings do not trigger YES. Why this could be too high: the evidence shows a fully built-out release plan and no hints of trouble, so the true probability may be closer to 1–2%. Why this could be too low: I lack current news on post-production status, the Warner Bros. Discovery corporate transition, exhibitor or labor disruptions, or any competitive re-slotting; a last-minute shift of even one week to avoid competition or for technical reasons would resolve YES, and packet limitations note placeholder text on the site, a minor signal of an unfinished web presence rather than the film itself.
limitations: Only a single supplied source (official site snapshot); no news coverage of post-production status, corporate developments, or exhibitor schedules as of the cutoff.
No fitted historical base rate for late-stage delays of major tentpoles; estimate relies on general background judgment.
Cannot verify whether the advertised date reflects a genuinely locked schedule versus stale marketing copy.
